title: Ironbark Pipeline Company and Sterling Bluff Water Department: crude oil release into the Kansas River
summary: A fictional crude oil pipeline operator, its oil spill removal cooperative and a downstream city water utility, with an exercise generated from their simulated plans: a morning release at a Kansas River crossing, notifications and Qualified Individual call-out, a Unified Command with EPA and the state, boom ahead of two water intakes, and a PREP exercise record.
notice: EXERCISE MATERIAL — for training use. Ironbark Pipeline Company, the response cooperative, Sterling Bluff, the water districts, people and sites are simulated; the public sources consulted for realism are listed in reference/pipeline-river-spill/SOURCES.md.

scenarios.title: Ditch to Intake
scenarios.summary: A leak alarm and a release of about 3,100 barrels of crude at the Kansas River crossing reaches the river in the morning; Ironbark must report, call out its Qualified Individual and OSRO, form a Unified Command, and get boom in place ahead of the Prairie Bend Rural Water District intake (about 5 hours downstream) and the Sterling Bluff intake (about 15 hours), while the water utility decides when to close its intake.
